statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk 12% (low) after the 22:00Z CME reopen printed an orderly near-flat gap, with NQZ26 up 0.22% at 31,130.25 and no range yet established, against Stress of 66% (high) as the Strait of Hormuz stays closed on Iran's seven stated conditions while flat oil and a 15.31 VIX show the weekend escalation stack was priced as a non-event.
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold, so the mapped policy state stays EA_ON. The narrow danger window is drawn across the 13:00-15:00Z block on 5 October, 15:00-17:00 Berlin, covering the US cash open and the September ISM Services PMI, where the published forecast Tail path peaks at 16% on scheduled-catalyst grounds rather than on observed one-way structure. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected by this state.
headline: Tail rises off its halt floor to 12% as the 22:00Z CME reopen prints an orderly 0.22% gap, while flat oil and a 15.31 VIX pull Stress down to 66%
body:
The CME equity-index reopen at 22:00Z has now been observed, and it resolved the main open question of the previous assessment. NQZ26 prints 31,130.25, up 68.50 points or 0.22% on a 31,061.75 prior close, with open, high and low still identical at that level on roughly 3,200 contracts. ESZ26 is up 7.25 points or 0.09% at 7,784.50 on roughly 3,700 contracts, and Sunday-evening reporting describes S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 futures each about 0.1% higher with attention on elevated Treasury yields and this week's FOMC minutes. A small gap that has produced no range at all is the opposite of the repeated-extension, no-retracement path Tail is designed to measure.

Tail therefore moves up from the 3% structural floor that applied while there was no tradeable price path, but only to 12%, which stays well inside the low band. The move up reflects the fact that a live price path now exists and is extremely thin rather than any observed pathology. The move is deliberately small because none of the amplifiers this contract requires is present: there is no persistent directional efficiency, no shallow-pullback sequence, no failed retracement and no session extreme being held, and the book has had barely half an hour to form a reference range.

Cross-assets argue against escalation pricing rather than for it. WTI trades 91.37 dollars, up 0.12% in a 91.26 to 91.85 range, and Brent is 102.91 dollars, down 0.06%, despite Houthi claims of ballistic-missile and drone strikes on Aramco facilities at Khurais and south of Riyadh, where flames and smoke were reported on Saturday afternoon with no formal Saudi confirmation and no reported production impact. Reporting also notes Middle Eastern crude flows have approached pre-war levels and that the G7 agreed to release up to 100 million barrels of reserves over four months. VIX closed Friday at 15.31, down 6.59% from 16.39 and near its 15.30 session low. Federal Reserve H.15 data for 1 October shows the 2-year at 4.78% and the 10-year at 5.24%, both lower on the day, with Friday's cash close reported higher at 4.837% and 5.279%. Low volatility, a flat crude complex and a bid equity tape is conflict, not the aligned amplifier stack Tail requires.

Stress eases four points to 66% precisely because the market has now had its chance to price the weekend. The 71% reading an hour ago rested on an escalation stack widening while the market was shut; that condition has been removed and the verdict was flat. The stack itself is unresolved: Iran rejected US counterproposals on denuclearisation, the parliament speaker restates that the strait stays closed until seven conditions are met, a commercial tanker was struck by an unknown projectile, Yemen's Presidential Council announced ground operations to retake Houthi-held territory, and US bombers were redeployed from RAF Fairford. Against that, Foreign Minister Araghchi says a seven-day plan could restore transit if diplomacy proceeds, and Iran's rial at a record low with a 2 billion dollar central-bank injection is pressure toward settlement rather than away from it. Elevated yields remain the durable background drag, which is a valuation headwind rather than a mean-reversion failure.

The published forecast keeps all 24 hours in EA_ON and green. Tail runs 12% to 13% through the thin Asian handoff, decays to a 9% to 10% range across the late Asian and European sessions, rebuilds to 10% into the US pre-market, steps to 14% for the 13:30Z cash open and the 13:45Z S&P Global services finals, peaks at 16% for the 14:00Z September ISM Services PMI, then eases to 10% to 11% across the afternoon, power hour and the 20:00Z cash close. No hour reaches the WATCH band, which is the disciplined reading of this contract: a scheduled release raises Stress and uncertainty first, and Tail follows only if the post-print path actually denies retracement. The danger window is drawn narrowly across the 13:00 to 15:00Z peak. Confidence is 85%, supported by live futures quotes from two independent sources, real-time crude, primary H.15 yields, verified incident reporting and a verified seven-day calendar, and held below the previous reading only because the live price path is half an hour old with no range. The shared Finviz context file was last collected on 29 September with a partial status, far outside the 90-minute freshness rule, so it was not used as evidence and this assessment rests entirely on independently verified sources.

lookbackSummary: Across the past 24 published hours Claude held Tail at 3% in every slot, mapping to EA_ON and green throughout with the dominant mode normal, because the CME equity-index complex was halted for the weekend and no Nasdaq-100 price path was scoreable. Stress rose from 70% at 22:00Z on 3 October to a 79% ceiling at 09:00Z on 4 October as the weekend Hormuz checkpoints and the Yemen and Saudi incident flow accumulated, then eased through the 73%, 70%, 68%, 66% and 64% readings of the European and US-equivalent hours before rebuilding into a 66% to 71% band across the Sunday evening ahead of the reopen. Confidence ran between 83% and 88%, improving through the Sunday hours as current levels, yields, oil and the forward calendar were re-verified while the live price path stayed structurally unavailable inside the halt.
outlookSummary: The current hour contains the observed 22:00Z reopen, which printed a 0.22% NQZ26 gap with no range on very thin volume, so Tail rises off its halt floor to 12% while Stress eases to 66% on a flat weekend repricing in oil and equity futures. Tail holds 12% to 13% through the thin Asian handoff, where a weekend headline remains the main discontinuity channel, then decays to a 9% to 10% range once Asian and European depth is established. It rebuilds to 10% into the US pre-market, steps to 14% for the 13:30Z cash open and 13:45Z S&P Global services finals, and peaks at 16% for the 14:00Z September ISM Services PMI, which the narrow 13:00 to 15:00Z danger window covers. That step is a scheduled-catalyst reading rather than observed one-way structure, and an orderly two-way reaction would invalidate it. Tail then eases to 10% to 11% through the afternoon, power hour and the 20:00Z cash close. Stress trends down from 66% to 59% by the end of the horizon and Confidence eases from 85% to 76% as distance from this assessment's evidence cutoff grows. Every published hour maps to EA_ON and green.

forecast.analysis: Liquidity should stay at its thinnest until Asian depth arrives, so a weekend headline landing in this hour could still move price discontinuously. Tail is nudged to 13% on that thin-book hazard alone; no one-way structure has been observed, and an orderly two-way range forming here would argue the gap risk has passed.

Unresolved Hormuz closure on Iran's seven stated conditions
Checkpoint: whether a genuine two-way range forms after the flat reopen

forecast.analysis: Tokyo comes in and begins setting the first real reference range off the reopen level. Tail holds at 13% while depth is still building: a rejected gap with a clean retracement toward 31,062 would be benign, whereas repeated extension away from the reopen print on improving volume would be the first genuine amplifier.
drivers: Tokyo open begins building the first reference range off the reopen
Invalidation: clean retracement toward the 31,061.75 prior close
Amplifier to watch: repeated extension on rising Asian volume

forecast.analysis: With Asian depth established a thin-book discontinuity becomes less likely and Tail eases to 11%. The regional conflict is unresolved, but the market's own weekend verdict was flat oil and flat equity futures, which under this contract informs Stress rather than Tail until a persistent directional path is observed.
drivers: Asian depth established, reducing thin-book discontinuity risk
Flat weekend repricing in oil and equity futures argues against aligned amplifiers
Hormuz closure remains unresolved as a discontinuity channel

forecast.analysis: A routine Asian hour. Tail settles to 10% as the dominant question becomes whether Friday's record cash close at 30,807.93 is accepted or faded in Asia. Orderly two-way trade is the base case; the conditional risk is an early Asian trend that holds its extremes into the European handover.
drivers: Acceptance or rejection of Friday's record 30,807.93 cash close
Base case: orderly two-way Asian trade
Conditional risk: Asian trend holding its extremes into Europe

forecast.analysis: Late Asian trade, typically the quietest stretch of the NQ day, and Tail stays at 10%. Elevated US yields near a 5.28% ten-year remain the most persistent structural headwind into the week, but a yield level by itself is a valuation drag rather than evidence of the mean-reversion failure Tail scores.
drivers: Ten-year near 5.28% as a persistent valuation headwind
Quietest stretch of the session historically
A yield level alone is not evidence of mean-reversion failure

forecast.analysis: Tail eases to 9% in the pre-European lull on the assumption that Asia closed without establishing one-way structure. If instead NQ is holding a session extreme by this hour with shallow pullbacks behind it, that assumption fails and the path would warrant a higher reading than the one published here.
drivers: Assumption: Asia ends without persistent directional efficiency
Invalidation: NQ holding a session extreme with shallow pullbacks
Pre-European lull in participation

forecast.analysis: Still ahead of the European cash open and Tail holds 9%. Overnight Middle East incident flow is the main discontinuity channel in this hour; Iran's rejection of US nuclear counterproposals keeps that channel open, while Araghchi's stated seven-day transit plan is the countervailing de-escalation path.
drivers: Overnight Middle East incident flow as the discontinuity channel
Iran rejected US nuclear counterproposals over the weekend

forecast.analysis: European pre-open. Tail stays at 9% because a cash-market handover is a liquidity event rather than an amplifier. The checkpoint is whether DAX and Euro Stoxx open in line with the flat US futures reopen or reprice the weekend escalation stack more aggressively than US futures chose to.
drivers: Checkpoint: European cash open in line with the flat futures reopen
A liquidity handover is not by itself a Tail amplifier

forecast.analysis: European cash trade is live and Tail is nudged to 10% for the added two-way flow. Cross-asset confirmation is the thing to watch: equities firm with Bunds and crude quiet would stay benign, whereas equities extending alongside a fresh yield and crude impulse would be the aligned stack this contract requires.

Benign read: equities firm with Bunds and crude quiet
Amplifier: equities extending alongside fresh yield and crude impulses

forecast.analysis: Mid-morning Europe and Tail holds 10%. The European session often sets the day's first durable range, so this hour is where persistent directional efficiency would first become measurable rather than merely assumed. Nothing published here asserts that such efficiency has appeared.
drivers: Europe often sets the first durable range of the day
First hour where directional efficiency becomes measurable

forecast.analysis: Tail stays at 10%. Attention through the European morning shifts toward the US calendar, with the September ISM Services PMI at 14:00Z the week's first scheduled checkpoint. forecast.analysis: European lunchtime, where participation typically thins and ranges compress, and Tail eases to 9%. A compressing range is the opposite of the repeated extension Tail scores, so absent a fresh catalyst this is among the lower-hazard hours of the published horizon.

An abnormal pre-open gap or a one-sided pre-market drift would be the first condition capable of lifting the published cash-open reading; a contained pre-market leaves it as drawn.
